question.prompt: If \(x\) is a real number, then the quantity \((1-|x|)(1+x)\) is positive if and only if

solutions.explanation:
A product is positive exactly when its factors have the same nonzero sign. Here the signs can change at \(x=-1\) and \(x=1\), where a factor is zero.

If \(x<-1\), then \(|x|>1\). Thus \(1-|x|<0\) and \(1+x<0\), so the product is positive.

If \(-1<x<1\), then \(|x|<1\). Both \(1-|x|\) and \(1+x\) are positive, so their product is positive.

If \(x>1\), then \(1-|x|<0\) while \(1+x>0\), so the product is negative. At \(x=-1\) and \(x=1\), the product is zero and is therefore excluded.

These cases cover all real numbers. The quantity is positive exactly when \(x<-1\) or \(-1<x<1\), choice E.
